subject: Meteorology
title: The World Meteorological Organization
description: A fast breakdown of The World Meteorological Organization for builders.

hook.text: Weather doesn't respect borders—international cooperation is essential, and the WMO coordinates it all.

buildup.text: The International Meteorological Organization was founded in 1873—replaced by the WMO in 1950 as a UN agency.

discovery.text: The WMO standardizes observation practices, codes, and instruments—so data from any country is usable by all.

twist.text: Even during the Cold War, the US and USSR freely shared weather data—forecasting required global cooperation.

climax.text: The World Weather Watch, launched in 1963, created a global observing and communication system still in operation today.

punchline.text: Nations that agree on little else agree on sharing weather data.

quiz.question: Why is international weather cooperation essential?
options: Weather doesn't respect borders—forecasting needs global data
